title: Trump suggests deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz may be imminent
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be announced soon, potentially as early as Wednesday. He described talks with Iran as "very good" and a "last chance." Trump also warned Iran would be "hit really hard" if no deal is reached. Meanwhile, a U.S. official indicated that temporary routes through the Strait would require no permits or fees, and no party would control navigation. Iran and Oman are reportedly working on a plan to reopen the waterway.
summary_points: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be announced soon, possibly by Wednesday.
Trump described talks with Iran as "very good" and a "last chance" for a deal.
Trump warned of severe consequences for Iran if a deal is not reached.
A U.S. official stated temporary routes through the Strait would be permit-free and fee-free, with no party controlling navigation.
Reports indicate Iran and Oman are collaborating on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
